output.contract_title: Software License Agreement with Enterprise Partner 012 LLC

clauses.clause_text: Customer shall pay all undisputed invoice amounts within thirty (30) days of invoice date.
Vendor shall notify Customer in writing within twenty-four (24) hours of becoming aware of any confirmed Data Breach.
Each party's maximum aggregate liability shall be strictly limited to the total fees paid under this Agreement in the preceding twelve (12) months.
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon providing thirty (30) days prior written notice.
This Agreement renews on an annual basis unless either party gives notice of non-renewal at least 30 days prior.

extraction_notes: Document extracted once for downstream policy comparison

mandatory_requirements.description: Aggregate liability cap must not exceed 12 months of total fees paid or payable.
mandatory_requirements.evaluation_criteria: Calculate total fees paid/payable over the contract term; liability cap must be less than or equal to twelve times the average monthly fee.

mandatory_requirements.description: Customer must have the right to terminate for convenience with no more than 30 days prior written notice.
mandatory_requirements.evaluation_criteria: Confirm contract includes a termination‑for‑convenience clause that permits the customer to give written notice of termination not exceeding 30 days.

ambiguities_in_policy.issue: Unclear definition of "total fees paid or payable" – does it include one‑time fees, future fees, taxes, or only recurring service fees?
Phrase "no more than 30 days" could be interpreted as a maximum notice period or as a minimum required notice; clarification is needed.

mappings.notes: Liability cap limited to total fees paid in the preceding twelve (12) months, directly meeting the 12‑month fee threshold.
Provides termination for convenience with thirty (30) days prior written notice; the right applies to the customer (and the other party).

risk_findings.ambiguity_description: The term "undisputed invoice amounts" is undefined, leaving uncertainty about payment obligations for disputed invoices and lacking a timeline or penalty for late payment of such amounts.
No payment deadline is specified for disputed invoice amounts, creating potential cash‑flow exposure.
"Confirmed Data Breach" is not defined; parties may disagree on what constitutes confirmation, delaying notification.
Requiring notification "in writing" within 24 hours may be impractical in emergency scenarios, risking non‑compliance and regulatory penalties.
Limiting aggregate liability to fees paid in the prior 12 months may be insufficient to cover consequential or regulatory damages, especially for data‑related breaches.
Termination for convenience with only 30‑day notice can cause abrupt service disruption; no transition or wind‑down obligations are defined.
Automatic annual renewal without specifying price adjustment mechanisms or notice requirements beyond a 30‑day non‑renewal notice may expose the customer to unexpected cost increases.

unresolved_questions: Definition of "undisputed invoice amounts" and handling of disputed invoices.
Acceptable formats for "in writing" notification (electronic vs. hard copy).
Mechanism for price adjustments upon renewal.
Whether the liability cap adequately covers regulatory or consequential damages.
Transition services or wind‑down obligations upon termination for convenience.
recommended_actions: Add a clear definition of "undisputed invoice amounts" and specify payment terms for disputed invoices, including any interest or penalty provisions.
Define "confirmed Data Breach" and consider allowing electronic notification (e.g., email) to satisfy the 24‑hour requirement.
Insert a clause describing acceptable notification methods (email, fax, portal) and record‑keeping requirements.
Introduce a price‑adjustment formula or index for renewal periods, or require mutual agreement on renewal pricing.
Re‑evaluate the liability cap; consider a higher cap or carve‑outs for data‑privacy, regulatory fines, and consequential damages.
Add transition‑service obligations (e.g., data migration, support continuity) and a wind‑down schedule for termination for convenience.
